title: Epistle of Barnabas, Chapter 21
language: Greek (Codex Sinaiticus) / English (J. B. Lightfoot, The Apostolic Fathers)
source: Codex Sinaiticus folio + transcription (codexsinaiticus.org) + J. B. Lightfoot, The Apostolic Fathers (1891)
description: Epistle of Barnabas chapter 21. Manuscript page scan(s) from Codex Sinaiticus hosted by the Codex Sinaiticus Project, with the Project's verbatim transcription of the Greek and the English of J. B. Lightfoot, The Apostolic Fathers (1891).
introduction:
This entry meets the strict three-criteria standard of the Theosis Library:

  1. Manuscript scan: The actual folio(s) of Codex Sinaiticus containing this chapter, from the Codex Sinaiticus Project (codexsinaiticus.org). Each section links to the specific folio holding its verses.
  2. Original text: The Codex Sinaiticus Project's verbatim transcription of the folio shown (uncial letters, lunate sigma, nomina sacra preserved).
  3. English translation: J. B. Lightfoot, The Apostolic Fathers (1891), public domain, retrieved verbatim from Lightfoot 1891 via earlychristianwritings.com transcription.

Why this is here: Codex Sinaiticus binds this text after Revelation, alongside the canonical books. Reading it on the same parchment as the Gospels is primary evidence for how a 4th-century Christian community treated it.

translation.original_text: <sup>1</sup>καλον εϲτιν μαθοντα τα δικαιωματα του κυ οϲα γεγραπται εν τουτοιϲ περιπατειν ο γαρ ταυτα ποιων εν τη βαϲιλεια του θυ δοξαϲθηϲεται ο εκεινα εκλεγομενοϲ μετα των εργων αυτου ϲυναπολιται δια τουτο αναϲταϲειϲ δια τουτο ανταποδομα <sup>2</sup>ερωτω τουϲ ϋπερεχοταϲ ει τινα μου γνωμηϲ αγαθηϲ λαμβανεται ϲυμβουλιαν εχετε μεθ εαυτων ειϲ ουϲ εργαϲηϲθε το καλον μη ενλιπηται <sup>3</sup>ενγυϲ η ημερα εν η ϲυναπολιται πατα τω πονηρω εγγυϲ ο κϲ και ο μιϲθοϲ αυτου <sup>4</sup>ετι και ετι ερωτω υμαϲ εαυτων γεινεϲθαι νομοθεται αγαθων εαυτω μενετε ϲυμβουλοι πιϲτοι αρα εξ υμων παρρηϲιαν ϋποκριϲιν <sup>5</sup>ο δε θϲ ο του παντοϲ κοϲμου κυριευων δωη υμιν ϲοφιαν ˙ ϲυνεϲιν · επιϲτημην · γνωϲιν των δικαιωματων αυτου υπομονην
translation.text: <sup>1</sup>It is good therefore to learn the ordinances of the Lord, as many as have been written above, and to walk in them. For he that doeth these things shall be glorified in the kingdom of God; whereas he that chooseth their opposites shall perish together with his works. For this cause is the resurrection, for this the recompense. <sup>2</sup>I entreat those of you who are in a higher station, if ye will receive any counsel of good advice from me, keep amongst you those to whom ye may do good. Fail not. <sup>3</sup>The day is at hand, in which everything shall be destroyed together with the Evil One. The Lord is at hand and his reward. <sup>4</sup>Again and again I entreat you; be good lawgivers one to another; continue faithful councilors to yourselves; take away from you all hypocrisy. <sup>5</sup>And may God, who is Lord of the whole world, give you wisdom, judgment, learning, knowledge of His ordinances, patience.

translation.original_text: <sup>6</sup>γιγνεϲθε δε εκζητουντεϲ τι ζητι κϲ αφ υμων και ποιειται ϊνα ευρεθηται εν ημερα κριϲεωϲ <sup>7</sup>ει δε τι εϲτιν αγαθου μνια μνημονευεται μου μελετωτεϲ ταυτα ϊνα και η επιθυμια και η αγρυπνια ειϲ τι αγαθον χωρηϲη ερωτω υμαϲ χαρι αιτουμενοϲ <sup>8</sup>εωϲ ετι το καλον ϲκευοϲ εϲτιν μεθ υμω μη ενλιπηται μηδενι εαυτων αλλα ϲυνεχωϲ εκζητιται ταυτα και αναπληρουται παϲαν εντολην εϲτιν γαρ αξια <sup>9</sup>διο μαλλο εϲπουδαϲα γραψε αφ ων ηδυνηθη ϲωζεϲθαι · αγαπηϲ τεκνα και ιρηνηϲ ο κϲ τηϲ δοξηϲ και παϲηϲ χαριτοϲ μετα του πνϲ ϋμων :
translation.text: <sup>6</sup>And be ye taught of God, seeking diligently what the Lord requireth of you, and act that ye may be found in the day of judgment. <sup>7</sup>But if you have any remembrance of good, call me to mind when ye practice these things these things, that both my desire and my watchfulness may lead to some good result. I entreat you asking it as a favor. <sup>8</sup>So long as the good vessel (of the body) is with you, be lacking in none of these things, but search them out constantly, and fulfill every commandment; for they deserve it. <sup>9</sup>For this reason I was the more eager to write to you so far as I was able, that I might give you joy. Fare ye well, children of love and peace. The Lord of glory and of every grace be with your spirit.
